label: a
rationale: Shared machinery: batch 1 develops group actions, stabilisers, transitivity, and geometric actions, while batch 9 develops Kan extensions, density, and free cocompletion. The bridge is concrete rather than merely thematic: batch 9's induction/coinduction examples for group representations and its orbit-category Kan extension use exactly the action-and-orbit viewpoint developed in batch 1. Keeping these pages together lets one Alpha check the stabiliser/orbit conventions against the categorical orbit and representation constructions. The run has no cross-batch dependency edges, so this genuine machinery link is the deciding criterion; the 103-item load is also moderate.

label: b
rationale: This is the algebraic-arithmetic cluster. Batch 2 studies integral binary quadratic forms under the SL_2(Z) action, discriminants, reduction, and class numbers; batch 3 supplies finite field extensions, norm and trace, Kummer theory, and solvability by radicals; batch 4 supplies localisation, tensor extension of scalars, exactness, and module support. The common checks are field/ring conventions, finite-extension and quotient constructions, group actions on algebraic data, and universal-property arguments. Batch 2 and batch 3 form the arithmetic link, while batch 3 and batch 4 form the field-to-module algebra link. This three-batch residual is within the cap and totals 119 items; no dependency edge can be saved by another arrangement because the facts report zero cross-batch edges.

label: c
rationale: Shared analytic machinery: batch 7 develops Lebesgue inner and outer measure, Vitali and Bernstein constructions, and the role of choice, while batch 8 develops Laurent residues, harmonic functions, Poisson kernels, and Dirichlet representation. The Poisson and harmonic arguments rely on the same real-variable integration and limiting conventions that batch 7 makes explicit, and batch 8's singularity and boundary examples provide analytic counterweight to batch 7's measurability boundaries. Keeping the two analytic pages together gives one reader the best chance to catch hidden measure, regularity, and choice hypotheses. Their combined load is 97 items.

label: d
rationale: The three combinatorics batches are kept whole because combinatorics is the only category with multiple batches and all three fit within one Alpha. The machinery is internally coherent: batch 5 develops combinatorial classes, generating functions, inversions and Eulerian statistics; batch 6 develops block designs, finite projective planes, and Erdős–Hajnal bounds; batch 10 develops polynomial Rödl, virality, and Erdős–Hajnal equivalence. The shared counting, extremal, homogeneous-set, and forbidden-configuration conventions are best checked by one reader, especially where batches 6 and 10 meet through Erdős–Hajnal language. The group has 124 items, a balanced load for the four-group partition.
